# Sign up pages: Request access

For internal systems without self sign-up: the employee sends national ID, employee number, work email, department and a reason, and an administrator approves the request. The panel explains what happens next.

A complete standalone component built only from `@mod-internal/ui`, Angular and plain CSS with the library tokens. Copy it, rename the selector and class, replace the sample text and data with the project's own (and its translation mechanism), and keep the structure.

export class RequestAccess {

  protected readonly form = new FormGroup({

    department: new FormControl('', { nonNullable: true, validators: Validators.required }),
    reason: new FormControl('', { nonNullable: true, validators: [Validators.required, Validators.minLength(20)] }),
  });
  protected readonly busy = signal(false);
  protected readonly failed = signal(false);
  /** Reference number returned by the server once the request is stored. */
  protected readonly reference = signal('');

  protected invalid(name: 'nationalId' | 'employeeNo' | 'email' | 'department' | 'reason'): boolean {
    const control = this.form.controls[name];
    return control.invalid && control.touched;
  }

  protected toggleLanguage(): void {
    const root = document.documentElement;
    root.dir = root.dir === 'rtl' ? 'ltr' : 'rtl';
  }

  protected async submit(): Promise<void> {
    this.failed.set(false);
    this.reference.set('');
    if (this.form.invalid) {
      this.form.markAllAsTouched();
      return;
    }
    this.busy.set(true);
    try {
      const request = this.form.getRawValue();
      // const { reference } = await this.access.request(request);
      // this.reference.set(reference);
      this.form.reset();
    } catch {
      this.failed.set(true);
    } finally {
      this.busy.set(false);
    }
  }
